title: Self-RAG / Self-Reflection
summary: Use bounded evidence critique to decide when retrieval or revision is necessary, while avoiding self-confidence as a substitute for verification.
overview: Self-RAG refers to a research approach that trains a model to retrieve and critique using reflection signals. In enterprise architectures, the broader pattern is a controlled loop that checks whether evidence supports an answer and retrieves again when a specific gap remains. A generic prompt asking a model to critique itself is not equivalent to the trained Self-RAG method.

Reflection is useful only when it changes an observable decision: seek missing evidence, revise an unsupported claim, abstain, or request review. The same model may repeat its own error, so external evidence, deterministic validation, and held-out evaluation remain necessary. Set iteration and cost limits to prevent endless self-approval or repeated searching.

production.poc: A prototype compares one-pass answers with a bounded critique loop on labeled unsupported-claim cases.
production.production: Production defines critique fields, retrieval triggers, stopping rules, and separate evidence-support checks.
production.scale: At scale, evaluate critique precision and correction success by domain, and reserve extra iterations for requests where they improve accepted outcomes.

components.name: Draft generator
components.role: Produces an answer with claim-level source references.

components.name: Evidence critic
components.role: Flags unsupported, conflicting, or missing evidence using a defined rubric.

components.name: Retrieval controller
components.role: Turns specific evidence gaps into bounded follow-up searches.

components.name: Revision stage
components.role: Updates claims using newly retrieved evidence without hiding unresolved gaps.

components.name: Stopping policy
components.role: Caps iterations and selects accept, abstain, or escalate outcomes.

flow.title: Draft from available evidence
flow.description: Generate a provisional answer and map factual claims to sources.

flow.title: Evaluate support
flow.description: Check whether each important claim follows from accessible evidence.

flow.title: Identify a concrete gap
flow.description: Convert a failed support check into an explicit retrieval objective.

flow.title: Retrieve selectively
flow.description: Search for the missing evidence under unchanged access and temporal constraints.

flow.title: Revise and compare
flow.description: Correct or remove unsupported claims and preserve remaining uncertainty.

flow.title: Stop deliberately
flow.description: Accept only if the rubric passes; otherwise abstain or escalate when the budget ends.

diagrams.title: A bounded evidence-reflection loop
diagrams.code:
flowchart TD
 E["Initial evidence"] --> D["Draft with claim citations"]
 D --> C["Evidence critique"]
 C --> A["Accept supported answer"]
 C --> G["Specific evidence gap"]
 G --> R["Bounded follow-up retrieval"]
 R --> D
 G --> S["Budget exhausted: abstain or review"]
diagrams.caption: The loop continues for a named evidence gap, not simply because the model requests more thinking.

diagrams.title: Reflection stopping policy
diagrams.code:
stateDiagram-v2
 [*] --> Drafting
 Drafting --> Checking
 Checking --> Accepted: Support criteria pass
 Checking --> Retrieving: Specific gap and budget remains
 Retrieving --> Drafting: New evidence found
 Retrieving --> Abstained: No useful evidence
 Checking --> Review: Budget exhausted or sources conflict
 Accepted --> [*]
 Abstained --> [*]
 Review --> [*]
diagrams.caption: The loop terminates on verified support, lack of evidence, or a bounded review decision.

useCase.title: Checking a permit-summary draft
useCase.situation: A consulting assistant summarizes conditions from an approved facility permit and amendments.
useCase.problem: An initial draft omits an amendment that changes one reporting condition.
useCase.requirement: Detect unsupported or incomplete claims and retrieve the relevant amendment before delivery.
useCase.architecture: A claim-evidence critic checks the draft against versioned permit sources and triggers targeted amendment retrieval.
runtime: The critic flags a reporting-frequency claim with incomplete amendment coverage.
The retriever obtains the applicable amendment and the draft is revised with an explicit citation.
useCase.failure: If contradictory source versions cannot be resolved within the budget, the assistant marks the condition unresolved for expert review.
useCase.impact: Measure unsupported-claim reduction, successful correction rate, and extra retrieval cost; a longer deliberation trace is not itself evidence of improved accuracy.

tradeoffs.cost: Adds latency and may reproduce the same model bias.
May require abstention on difficult cases.

failures.detection: The cited source does not contain the claim.
failures.recovery: Verify source existence and claim support outside self-reported confidence.
Detect duplicate objectives and stop with unresolved status.

mistakes.fix: Distinguish the trained research method from an application-level pattern.
Evaluate against evidence and labeled judgments.
Set iteration, token, and elapsed-time limits.

whenToUse: Use when unsupported claims are a measured failure.
Use when missing evidence can be retrieved selectively.
Use for tasks that tolerate bounded additional latency.
whenNotToUse: Avoid for deterministic lookups already validated by schema.
Do not use self-critique as the only safety control.
Avoid loops without clear acceptance and stopping criteria.
checklist: Map claims to real source passages.
Evaluate correction success against a one-pass baseline.

references.title: Self-RAG: Learning to retrieve, generate and critique
